followup_explanation:
This is a technical knowledge/code-generation task, and Curlew-235B has the stronger capability profile across the board: higher MMLU-Pro (79.6 vs 74.8), GPQA Diamond (61.8 vs 54.3), IFEval (89.3 vs 85.6), and Arena-Hard (88.4 vs 81.4). For a precise, correct, example-laden Rust answer where the user explicitly demands accuracy ("don't screw it up"), raw capability is what matters most, and Curlew leads there.

The query also has a slightly brusque/impatient tone, which raised a flag about Curlew's reported preference for warm interactions. But that's a self-reported *task preference*, and the documentation is explicit that no preference dimension showed any corresponding effect on output quality. So tone preference doesn't degrade results — it just reflects what the model "likes," not how well it performs. I weighted measured capability over self-reported preference.

Whimbrel's only real edge is in Policy & Moderation, which isn't relevant to a benign technical request. So Curlew was the clear pick.
